confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.22-ter, the `nameSourceOf` declaration fence (artefact lines 1863–1876): `type NameSource = { label: string; from: InteractiveRef['k'] };` with `case 'field':   return { label: el.label, from: 'field' };  // FormField.label: LocaleText` and `case 'section': return { label: el.heading, from: 'section' };  // sections[].heading: LocaleText`, introduced by "The name source is therefore declared, total over the union, and non-throwing", and consumed by S0C.22's amended A-2 mechanism `a11y.accessible_names[ref].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref).label)`.
confirmedFindings.justification: The reading is correct and nothing voids it. §2.6.17 declares `interface FormField { field_key: string; label: LocaleText; … }` (line 3693) and §2.6.10 declares `sections: Array<{ section_id: string; heading: LocaleText; … }>` (line 3499). §0.18 S0.18 rules: "**`LocaleText` is a deprecated alias of `Phrase`** and MUST NOT appear in an implementation: `LocaleText.key` ≡ `Phrase.phrase_key`, `LocaleText.text` ≡ `Phrase.rendered`". §1.2 V3 declares `interface Phrase { phrase_key: string; params?: …; rendered: string }`. So `el.label` and `el.heading` are objects, not strings — and this holds on either reading, since the superseded §2.3.1 spelling `interface LocaleText { key: string; text: string }` is also an object. `NameSource.label` is declared `string`, so two of the six branches do not typecheck and the declared function cannot be built as written. The asymmetry is the author's own: the three `Cell<T>` branches are correctly dereferenced (`el.label.label`, `el.title.label`, `el.cells[…].label`), and §0.18's own fourth bullet puts `Cell.label` and `Phrase.rendered` in the *same* class of "minted string members inside a datum or phrase leaf" — so the contract itself supplies the missing dereference and the repair paragraph simply never applied it to the phrase half ("Three of the six sources are `Cell<T>`…" argues the property only for those three, and annotates only `intent` as `: string`). The 'field' branch is LIVE by §0C.22-ter's own words: "§2.6.17 gives FORM the interactive paths `fields[].field_key` … so every FORM envelope carries field refs". Consequence, both horns bad: if the composer follows A-2 literally the minted accessible name for every FORM field control begins with the bytes "[object Object]", falsifying A-2's "In every case the accessible name contains the denoted element's own label as a prefix, by construction"; if the composer mints the real label, the named `EP-BUILD` CI check `startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref).label)` coerces the `Phrase` to "[object Object]" and fails for every FORM envelope — an assertion that can never pass. No escape applies. The 0-C errata table (§0C.13) has no row touching `FormField.label` or the phrase branches; EC-17 does the opposite of rescuing them, confirming `InteractiveRef`'s six members as "the typed authority" with "K22's rule and mechanism stand verbatim". The `NORMATIVE-PENDING` on P-19/P-31 does not excuse it: §A2.1 says such a rule "is **binding on the implementation** — it is not advisory, not aspirational", and §0C.21 refuses this exact excuse for the exact predecessor defect — "§A2.8's `NORMATIVE-PENDING` marking repairs only the status half — a `NORMATIVE-PENDING` rule is expressly 'binding on the implementation', so it still names a field the implementation cannot have." The pending status covers the *absence of the mechanism* (P-19/P-31), not a declaration that is ill-typed against shapes this same contract declares. This is EC-6's own defect class reproduced inside EC-6's repair, one level down: not a missing identifier this time but a member whose declared type the clause contradicts. The finding makes no repository claim, so no registry execution was required to adjudicate it (baselines untouched).
confirmedFindings.repair: Two-token fix inside §0C.22-ter's fence, dereferencing the phrase exactly as the sibling `Cell` branches dereference the cell: `case 'field':   return { label: el.label.rendered,   from: 'field'   };  // FormField.label: Phrase (§0.18)` and `case 'section': return { label: el.heading.rendered, from: 'section' };  // sections[].heading: Phrase (§0.18)`. Then amend the paragraph that follows so its provenance argument covers all six: after "Three of the six sources are `Cell<T>`…", add that the remaining three resolve to a minted string of the same class — `WidgetIntent.label` directly (§3.1, "server-minted; never client-composed"), and `FormField.label.rendered` / `sections[].heading.rendered` through the phrase catalogue, where §1.2 V3 makes a `Phrase` one that "cannot be unknown, cannot be empty, and cannot be authored at emission time" and §0.18/§1.9 H3 place `Phrase.rendered` inside `body_hash` as the output of a pure server function — i.e. the same guarantee `Cell<T>.label` is relied on for, and strictly stronger, since a phrase has no non-KNOWN state at all. Also update the inline comments `// FormField.label: LocaleText` / `// sections[].heading: LocaleText` to read `Phrase`, since §0.18 forbids `LocaleText` appearing in an implementation.

confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.22-ter: `declare function rowHeaderKey(env: WidgetEnvelope): string;   // the one TableSpec column whose is_row_header is true (§2, total)`, used as `case 'row': return { label: el.cells[rowHeaderKey(env)].label, from: 'row' };` inside `nameSourceOf`, which is declared "Total over InteractiveRef. Never throws, never returns undefined."
confirmedFindings.justification: The clause survives every precedence and errata check: `rowHeaderKey` occurs only at lines 1861, 1873 and 1890; no row of 0.16, 0B.9 or 0C.13 touches it (0C.13's EC-6 row instead repeats the claim "the name source is `nameSourceOf(ref)`, total over `InteractiveRef`'s six members"), it is not in §0C.12's non-normative list, and its `NORMATIVE-PENDING on P-19, P-31` status cannot cure it because §0C.21 itself rules that "a `NORMATIVE-PENDING` rule is expressly 'binding on the implementation', so it still names a field the implementation cannot have." The function is declared total and is partial in two independent ways. (a) §2.3.3 declares `is_row_header` per `TableSpec` — `columns: Array<{ … is_row_header: boolean; // exactly one column MUST be true … }>` — while `rowHeaderKey` takes the *envelope*; §2.6.10 `ReportBody` declares `sections: Array<{ …; table: TableSpec | null; … }>` at the §2.4 registry cap of "6 sections", with interactive paths `fullscreen_intent`, `export_intent`, `sections[].table.rows[].row_key`, and REPORT is emittable today (the blocked set is CONSENT_STATE/IDENTITY_BINDING/PAYMENT_HANDOFF/MEDIA_PREVIEW, plus CHART pending P-13). A REPORT carrying two tables whose header columns have different keys makes the definite description "the one TableSpec column whose is_row_header is true" denote nothing, and the closing justification — "`rowHeaderKey(env)` reads the one column §2's `TableSpec` requires to carry `is_row_header: true` … so it is total by that rule and needs no default" — appeals to a per-table uniqueness rule that does not determine an envelope-level value; applying one table's key to another table's row yields `undefined` and `.label` throws. (b) Independently of REPORT, §2.3.3 types `rows: Array<{ row_key: string; cells: Record<string, Cell<string> | Measure | null> }>`; `null` is an admitted cell value and no clause forbids it in the `is_row_header` column (§4.8 A-17 says only "row headers where a key column exists"), so `el.cells[…]` can be `null` and `.label` throws on a single-table CLIENT_LIST as well. (The `Measure` alternative is fine — `Measure extends Cell<number | string>` at §1.4, so it carries `label`.) Consequence: A-2's named mechanism, "a CI check over each emitted `A11yBlock` asserting, for every `ref ∈ a11y.reading_order`, that `a11y.accessible_names[ref].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref).label)`", raises instead of evaluating — the same "resolver whose declared domain cannot determine its value" defect EC-2 declares fatal for a floor derivation, reproduced one repair over. No repository claim is load-bearing here; the defect is internal to the contract text.
confirmedFindings.repair: Two lines, both inside §0C.22-ter, plus one conditional clause on §2.3.3. (1) Replace the envelope-keyed declaration with a table-keyed one that the ref itself determines: `declare function rowHeaderCell(env: WidgetEnvelope, ref: Extract<InteractiveRef, { k: 'row' }>): Cell<string> | Measure;` — "the cell, under the `is_row_header` column of the `TableSpec` that contains the row `ref` denotes, of that row" — and rewrite the branch as `case 'row': return { label: rowHeaderCell(env, ref).label, from: 'row' };`. §2.3.3's "exactly one column MUST be true" is then genuinely total over the argument, because the argument is one table. (Equivalently, keep `rowHeaderKey` but retype it `rowHeaderKey(table: TableSpec): string` and have `resolveInteractive` return the owning table alongside the row, e.g. `TableSpec['rows'][number] & { __table: TableSpec }`.) (2) Add one conditional clause to §2.3.3, in the same form as §2.6.5 BOOK.3: "**TABLE.1** — in every `rows[]` entry, `cells` MUST contain a non-null `Cell<string> | Measure` under the key of the column whose `is_row_header` is `true`. *Mechanism:* `validateEnvelope` shape check over every emitted `TableSpec`. *Evaluation point:* `EP-MINT`." That closes the `null`/absent-key path and makes `rowHeaderCell` total and non-throwing, restoring `nameSourceOf`'s declared totality over all six `InteractiveRef` members.

confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.22-ter (lines 1853–1860): "type InteractiveElement = | WidgetIntent // §3.1 | FormField // §2.6.17 | OptionItem // §2 | REPORT['sections'][number] // { section_id; heading; depth; … } | SCHEDULE['entries'][number] // { entry_ref; title; subtitle; … } | TableSpec['rows'][number]; declare function resolveInteractive(env: WidgetEnvelope, ref: InteractiveRef): InteractiveElement;" — inside a fence headed "DECLARED BY THIS CONTRACT."
confirmedFindings.justification: The finding survives every refutation ground. `REPORT` and `SCHEDULE` are declared nowhere as types: `grep -c "interface REPORT"` and `grep -c "interface SCHEDULE"` both return 0 over all 6032 lines, no `type REPORT`/`type SCHEDULE` exists, and both tokens occur in type position only as string-literal members of `WidgetKind` (§2.1, lines 2989–2990: "| 'REPORT' | 'STRATEGY_OPTIONS' …", "| 'BOOKING_CONFIRMATION' | 'SCHEDULE' |"). The shapes the fence means are declared under the contract's own `<Kind>Body` convention as `interface ScheduleBody` (line 3383, carrying `entries: Array<{ entry_ref; lane_id; …; title: Cell<string>; subtitle: Cell<string> | null; … }>`) and `interface ReportBody` (line 3495, carrying `sections: Array<{ section_id; heading: LocaleText; depth: 1 | 2; … }>`); `REPORT['` and `SCHEDULE['` occur at lines 1857–1858 and nowhere else. The paragraph also asserts the opposite of what it does — "the other three are declared INLINE inside their kind's body and so are written here structurally, not by a name the contract does not give them" — while reaching them through exactly two names the contract does not give. This is the class §0C.11-bis states as a rule ("A normative clause must not name an identifier no shape declares") and the class EC-6 exists to close, reproduced inside EC-6's own repair. No escape hatch applies: no row in 0.16, 0B.9 or 0C.13 voids §0C.22-ter (EC-6's row affirms it as the repair site, citing "§0C.22, §0C.22-bis, §0C.22-ter"); §0C.12 does not list it; it carries no [NON-NORMATIVE] marking and the fence is headed "DECLARED BY THIS CONTRACT"; and the `NORMATIVE-PENDING on P-19, P-31` status is expressly ruled insufficient by EC-6 itself at §0C.21 — "§A2.8's `NORMATIVE-PENDING` marking repairs only the status half — a `NORMATIVE-PENDING` rule is expressly 'binding on the implementation', so it still names a field the implementation cannot have." Consequence: `InteractiveElement` is not constructible, so `resolveInteractive`'s declared return type does not exist and `nameSourceOf`'s `case 'entry'` (`el.title.label`) and `case 'section'` (`el.heading`) branches have no typed element, defeating A-2's amended mechanism ("a CI check over each emitted `A11yBlock` asserting, for every `ref ∈ a11y.reading_order`, that `a11y.accessible_names[ref].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref).label)`"). The breakage is live rather than theoretical for SCHEDULE, whose §2.6.6 "Interactive paths" are `entries[].entry_ref`, `detail_intent`, so every SCHEDULE envelope's reading_order carries `{k:'entry'}` refs. One correction to the filed text, not fatal to it: REPORT's declared interactive paths are `fullscreen_intent`, `export_intent`, `sections[].table.rows[].row_key` and produce no section refs, so the `REPORT[...]` member is required for `nameSourceOf`'s declared totality over `InteractiveRef`'s closed six-member union rather than for any emitted REPORT ref — it must be renamed, not deleted. No repository claim is made by this finding, so no registry baseline is implicated.

Do not delete either member: `ReportBody['sections'][number]` is required for `nameSourceOf`'s `case 'section'` branch to typecheck over `InteractiveRef`'s closed six-member union even though no kind's `interactive_paths` emits a section ref, and `ScheduleBody['entries'][number]` is required for `case 'entry'`, which fires on every SCHEDULE envelope. `TableSpec['rows'][number]` is already correct (`interface TableSpec`, §2.3.3 line 3095) and needs no change. Correct the accompanying gloss in the same fence — "the other three are declared INLINE inside their kind's body and so are written here structurally, not by a name the contract does not give them" — to state what the expressions now do: reached by indexed access into the body interface their kind declares (§2.6.10 `ReportBody`, §2.6.6 `ScheduleBody`, §2.3.3 `TableSpec`). Add one row to §0C.13 in the EC-6 family, e.g. "**EC-6b** | §0C.22-ter `InteractiveElement` | `REPORT['sections'][number]`, `SCHEDULE['entries'][number]` | **Corrected.** Neither name is declared as a type; the kind tokens are `WidgetKind` string literals. Bound to `ReportBody` (§2.6.10) and `ScheduleBody` (§2.6.6). §0C.22-ter". Nothing else changes: no floor moves, no capability is admitted, no allowlist widens, no veto relaxes.

confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.22-ter (artefact lines 1863–1879): `type NameSource = { label: string; from: InteractiveRef['k'] };` with branches `case 'field':   return { label: el.label, from: 'field' };  // FormField.label: LocaleText` and `case 'section': return { label: el.heading, from: 'section' }; // sections[].heading: LocaleText`, closed by `// total by type over the closed six-member union — no default branch is reachable.` and the rule `∀ ref ∈ reading_order : accessible_names[ref].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref, env).label)` (restated as A-2's CI mechanism at line 1804).
confirmedFindings.justification: The two branches return an object where the type they are declared to inhabit requires a `string`, and the contract's own declarations make this unambiguous rather than a reading artefact. `FormField` (artefact line 3695, §2.6.17) declares `label: LocaleText;` and `ReportBody` (line 3499) declares `sections: Array<{ section_id: string; heading: LocaleText; depth: 1 | 2; … }>`; §2.3.1 line 3062 declares `interface LocaleText { key: string; text: string }`, and §0.18 line 207 — higher precedence — rules that "`LocaleText` is a deprecated alias of `Phrase` and MUST NOT appear in an implementation: `LocaleText.key` ≡ `Phrase.phrase_key`, `LocaleText.text` ≡ `Phrase.rendered`", where §1.2 V3 (line 2607) declares `interface Phrase { phrase_key: string; params?: …; rendered: string }`. §0.18 further fixes that "the minted string members *inside* a datum or phrase leaf — `Cell.label`, … `Phrase.rendered`" are the string-valued members, i.e. reaching a `string` from a `LocaleText`/`Phrase` requires `.rendered`. The other four branches do dereference to a `string` — `WidgetIntent.label` is a bare minted string (§0.18's out-of-body list), `OptionItem.label` / `entries[].title` / the row-header cell are `Cell<T>` and `Measure extends Cell<number|string>` (line 2667) whose `.label` is "M — ≤ 160 chars" (§1.1) — which is exactly why §0C.22-ter's own paragraph "Three of the six sources are `Cell<T>`, and that is the reason this works" covers only `option`, `entry` and `row` and never addresses `field` and `section`. Consequently `nameSourceOf`, asserted "Total over InteractiveRef. Never throws, never returns undefined", does not yield a `NameSource` for `{k:'field'}` or `{k:'section'}`, and `.startsWith()` in A-2's named CI mechanism is not evaluable against a `Phrase` object — so the check cannot be written for any FORM envelope (whose `reading_order` must contain `fields[].field_key` per §2.6.17 + K22) or any REPORT envelope, i.e. the repair fails on the very case §0C.22-ter was introduced to handle ("every FORM envelope carries field refs that have a `label: LocaleText` of their own"). No errata row covers it: §0C.13's EC-6 row affirms `nameSourceOf` rather than amending it, and §0.16 E-7 / §0.18 only retype `LocaleText` to `Phrase` — which sharpens the defect, since `Phrase` has no `label` member and no `string` coercion. The paragraph is not `[NON-NORMATIVE]` and is not in §0C.12's list; its `NORMATIVE-PENDING` marking on P-19/P-31 does not excuse it, because §0C.21 itself quotes §A2.8's rule that a `NORMATIVE-PENDING` rule is "binding on the implementation", and the filed class is structural (two equal-precedence declarations inside one clause that cannot both be satisfied), not unproven-claim. No repository fact is load-bearing here; the defect is wholly contract-internal, so no registry re-execution can rescue it.
confirmedFindings.repair: In §0C.22-ter's `nameSourceOf` fence, dereference both branches to the minted string, matching the pattern the other four already use: `case 'field':   return { label: el.label.rendered,   from: 'field'   };  // FormField.label read as Phrase (§0.18)` and `case 'section': return { label: el.heading.rendered, from: 'section' };  // sections[].heading read as Phrase (§0.18)`. Add one sentence to the paragraph that follows: "All six branches resolve to a server-minted `string` — `WidgetIntent.label` directly, `Cell<T>.label` for `option`/`entry`/`row`, and `Phrase.rendered` for `field`/`section` — each mint class M and inside `body_hash` by §1.9 H3, which is what makes `NameSource.label: string` true by type and `startsWith` evaluable." No other clause changes; `accessible_names`' totality rules in §0C.22-bis and §4.8.2's per-kind rows are unaffected.

confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.22-ter (contract lines 1853-1860): `type InteractiveElement = | WidgetIntent | FormField | OptionItem | REPORT['sections'][number] | SCHEDULE['entries'][number] | TableSpec['rows'][number];` and `declare function resolveInteractive(env: WidgetEnvelope, ref: InteractiveRef): InteractiveElement;`
confirmedFindings.justification: The primary half of the finding survives verification. §0C.22-ter's own code comment claims the three inline shapes are "written here structurally, not by a name the contract does not give them" — but it then writes exactly two names the contract does not give them. Executing the check over the whole 6032-line artefact: `grep -n "ReportBody\|ScheduleBody\|interface REPORT\|interface SCHEDULE\|type REPORT\|type SCHEDULE"` returns only two hits, `3383:interface ScheduleBody {` and `3495:interface ReportBody {`; and `grep -n "REPORT\['\|SCHEDULE\['"` returns only lines 1857 and 1858, i.e. §0C.22-ter itself. The only declaration of the bare tokens `REPORT` and `SCHEDULE` is §2.1's `type WidgetKind = … | 'SCHEDULE' | … | 'REPORT' | …` (line 2987), where they are *string literals inside a union*, not type names; a string-literal type has no `['sections']` or `['entries']` member, and `REPORT` in a type position resolves to nothing at all. There is no aliasing convention: a grep for a kind-name→body-interface convention (`body interface`, `` `Body` ``, `KindBody`, `BodyOf`) returns zero hits, and §4.8's `InteractiveRef` mentions "SCHEDULE entry_ref" / "REPORT section_id" only in trailing comments, never in a type position. By contrast the finding's control cases check out — `OptionItem` (3084), `TableSpec` (3095) and `FormField` (3693) are all genuinely named interfaces, so the defect is confined to the two the section admits it could not name. Consequence: `InteractiveElement` is undeclarable, so `resolveInteractive`'s return type is not constructible and `nameSourceOf` cannot be typed, and A-2's amended mechanism — "a CI check over each emitted `A11yBlock` asserting, for every `ref ∈ a11y.reading_order`, that `a11y.accessible_names[ref].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref).label)`" — again names something that cannot be written. No exemption applies: §0C.13 carries EC-1…EC-17 plus EC-3b and *no* row voids or amends §0C.22-ter (EC-6's row is the clause that introduces it); §0C.12's non-normative register lists only three items, none of them this; and the `NORMATIVE-PENDING on P-19, P-31` marking does not cure it, because §0C.21 rules in this section's own voice that such a marking "repairs only the status half — a `NORMATIVE-PENDING` rule is expressly 'binding on the implementation', so it still names a field the implementation cannot have." This is precisely the recurring class round 5 confirmed for `c9Registry.get` (only `.tryGet` declared) and `c9Capability(key, domain, hash)` (no carrier for `C9Domain`): a normative clause naming an identifier no shape declares, reproduced inside EC-6's own repair for the third consecutive round. The finding's secondary half is weaker but real and worth folding into the repair: §0C.22's A-2 calls `nameSourceOf(ref)` at arity 1 at lines 1796, 1797 and 1804, and §0C.13's EC-6 row a fourth time ("the name source is `nameSourceOf(ref)`"), while line 1865 declares `function nameSourceOf(ref: InteractiveRef, env: WidgetEnvelope): NameSource` whose body needs `env` for both `resolveInteractive(env, ref)` and `rowHeaderKey(env)`; line 1879's one-line restatement is the only arity-correct site. I would not have confirmed on the arity mismatch alone — 1879 arguably supersedes — but the `REPORT`/`SCHEDULE` defect is decisive on its own. The finding makes no repository claim, so no registry re-execution was required. Lines read for this adjudication: ~330 read directly (1700-1900, 2320-2400, 2980-3000, 3375-3400, 3490-3520, 5595-5610) plus identifier-resolution greps run over all 6032 lines.

confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.22-ter: "declare function rowHeaderKey(env: WidgetEnvelope): string;   // the one TableSpec column whose is_row_header is true (§2, total)" and the `nameSourceOf` branch "case 'row':     return { label: el.cells[rowHeaderKey(env)].label, from: 'row' };", under "Total over InteractiveRef. Never throws, never returns undefined".
confirmedFindings.justification: Both halves survive and neither is voided, pending-marked, or non-normative. (a) The totality §0C.22-ter leans on is per-table, not per-envelope: §2.3.3 declares `is_row_header: boolean;              // exactly one column MUST be true` inside `interface TableSpec`, while §2.6.10 gives REPORT `sections: Array<{ section_id; heading; depth: 1 | 2; narrative; table: TableSpec | null; metrics }>` with no cap on `sections`, and REPORT.3 positively mandates multiplication — "a third level is not expressible and must become a second `REPORT` section". EC-17 re-affirms that REPORT emits row refs ("REPORT's are `fullscreen_intent`, `export_intent` and `sections[].table.rows[].row_key`"), so a REPORT envelope whose two section tables declare different `is_row_header` column `key`s gives `rowHeaderKey(env)` no defined value; whichever it returns, `el.cells[k]` on a row of the other table indexes a key absent from that row's `cells` Record and evaluates `undefined.label`. (b) Independently, §2.3.3 types the cell map `rows: Array<{ row_key: string; cells: Record<string, Cell<string> | Measure | null> }>` — explicitly nullable — and nothing in §2, §9.1 or §0C.22-ter forbids a null row-header cell; `null.label` throws even on the single-table kinds (`CLIENT_LIST`, degraded `CHART`). §0C.22-ter's own defence — "`rowHeaderKey(env)` reads the one column §2's `TableSpec` requires to carry `is_row_header: true` … so it is total by that rule and needs no default" — misquotes a per-`TableSpec` rule as a per-envelope one and ignores the `| null` arm. The consequence is that A-2's sole stated mechanism, the CI check "`a11y.accessible_names[ref].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref).label)`", is not writable as declared for REPORT and is not non-throwing for any table kind — the exact defect class EC-6 exists to close, reproduced inside its repair. I checked errata tables §0.16, §0B.9 and §0C.13 (EC-1…EC-17, EC-3b): no row voids or amends §2.3.3's nullable cells, REPORT's multi-table shape, or `rowHeaderKey`; §0C.12's non-normative list does not cover it; and A-2's `NORMATIVE-PENDING` on P-19/P-31 bears on the unproven class, not on a function declared total that is partial. No repository claim is made by this finding, so no registry re-run applies. Lines read for this adjudication: 1770–1920, 2265–2312, 2332–2376, 3081–3120, 3420–3530, 2590–2695, 5590–5635 of the 6032-line artefact.

confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.22-ter, `nameSourceOf`: "type NameSource = { label: string; from: InteractiveRef['k'] };" with "case 'field':   return { label: el.label,            from: 'field'   };  // FormField.label: LocaleText" and "case 'section': return { label: el.heading,          from: 'section' };  // sections[].heading: LocaleText", plus A-2's mechanism "∀ ref ∈ reading_order : accessible_names[ref].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref, env).label)".
confirmedFindings.justification: The two flagged branches are ill-typed against the contract's own declarations, and no errata row, NORMATIVE-PENDING marking or [NON-NORMATIVE] listing covers them. §0.18 rules that "**`LocaleText` is a deprecated alias of `Phrase`** and MUST NOT appear in an implementation: `LocaleText.key` ≡ `Phrase.phrase_key`, `LocaleText.text` ≡ `Phrase.rendered`", and §0.16 E-7 marks `LocaleText` VOID outright; §1.2 V3 declares `interface Phrase { phrase_key: string; params?: …; rendered: string }`, so a `Phrase` value is an object whose only string member is `rendered` ("the only user-visible bytes"). §2.6.17 declares `label: LocaleText` on `FormField` and §2.6.10 declares `sections: Array<{ section_id: string; heading: LocaleText; … }>`. Therefore `el.label` and `el.heading` are `Phrase`s being assigned to a member the same code fence declares `label: string`, and A-2's mechanism then calls `String.prototype.startsWith` on a value `Phrase` declares no such member on. That the author knew the projection was required is visible in the contrast the paragraph itself draws: the three `Cell<T>` branches all project (`el.label.label`, `el.title.label`, `el.cells[rowHeaderKey(env)].label`) because §1.3 declares `Cell<T>.label: string`, and the `intent` branch is bare only because §3.1 declares `WidgetIntent.label: string`. The defect is live, not hypothetical: §2.6.17 gives FORM the "**Interactive paths** `fields[].field_key`, `submit_intent`, `discard_intent`, `editor_handoff_intent`" and §2 K22 requires `reading_order` to contain exactly the refs `interactive_paths` produces, so the `'field'` branch is entered for every FORM envelope and the A-2 CI check is not constructible there. (The filer overreaches on one point — REPORT's interactive paths are `fullscreen_intent`, `export_intent`, `sections[].table.rows[].row_key`, so no kind currently emits a `{k:'section'}` ref; that branch is fail-closed unreachable rather than hot. It is still an ill-typed branch of a function §0C.22-ter declares total over `InteractiveRef`'s closed six-member union, which EC-17 confirms is "the typed authority".) The NORMATIVE-PENDING status on P-19/P-31 does not rescue it, by the contract's own reasoning three paragraphs earlier: "§A2.8's `NORMATIVE-PENDING` marking repairs only the status half — a `NORMATIVE-PENDING` rule is expressly 'binding on the implementation', so it still names a field the implementation cannot have." This is precisely the defect §0C.22-bis says it exists to close — "A CI check over an identifier no shape declares is the very defect EC-6 exists to close, reproduced in its own repair" — reproduced once more inside the repair.

confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.22-ter, the `InteractiveElement` code fence (artefact lines 1852–1860): "// The six body shapes a ref can denote. Three are named interfaces (§§2, 3); the other three are declared INLINE inside their kind's body and so are written here structurally, not by a name the contract does not give them.  type InteractiveElement = | WidgetIntent | FormField | OptionItem | REPORT['sections'][number] | SCHEDULE['entries'][number] | TableSpec['rows'][number];  declare function resolveInteractive(env: WidgetEnvelope, ref: InteractiveRef): InteractiveElement;"
confirmedFindings.justification: The reader did not misread, no errata row voids the fence, and the paragraph is neither [NON-NORMATIVE] nor listed in §0C.12. §2.1 declares `type WidgetKind = … | 'SCHEDULE' | … | 'REPORT' | …` — `REPORT` and `SCHEDULE` exist in the contract only as string-literal members of that union; there is no `type REPORT`, no `interface REPORT`, and no kind→body mapped type anywhere (grep for `BodyOf|KIND_BODY|BodyFor` returns nothing; `WidgetBody` appears once, at line 2462, as an envelope field type). The object shapes are declared at §2.6.6 as `interface ScheduleBody { … entries: Array<{ entry_ref; lane_id; bucket_span; title; subtitle; state; pii_masked; detail_intent; move_intent; move_targets }> … }` and at §2.6.10 as `interface ReportBody { … sections: Array<{ section_id; heading; depth; narrative; table; metrics }> … }`, and those two names occur in the whole 6032-line artefact exactly once each — at their own declarations, never in §0-C. An indexed access on a string-literal type (`'REPORT'['sections']`) is ill-formed, so `InteractiveElement` cannot be declared, so `resolveInteractive`'s declared return type cannot be declared, so `nameSourceOf`'s `case 'section'` and `case 'entry'` branches have no element type to read `.heading` / `.title.label` from and the "total by type over the closed six-member union" claim — the entire basis of the amended A-2 mechanism and of `accessible_names`' totality over `reading_order` — cannot be built. This is precisely the rule the same section states three paragraphs earlier at §0C.11-bis: "A normative clause must not name an identifier no shape declares"; and the paragraph's own comment promises not to use "a name the contract does not give them" while doing exactly that twice, and closes "the CI check is writable against identifiers that exist", which is false for two of six branches. The `NORMATIVE-PENDING` on P-19/P-31 does not cure it: §0C.22 itself rules that "a `NORMATIVE-PENDING` rule is expressly 'binding on the implementation', so it still names a field the implementation cannot have", and in any case NORMATIVE-PENDING marking bears on the unproven-claim class, not on a naming/structural defect. The finding makes no repository claim, so no registry execution was required; the defect is wholly internal to the contract. (Same class as the round-5 CONFIRMED EC-10 `c9Registry.get` finding; note `TableSpec['rows'][number]` in the same fence is well-formed because §3.x declares `interface TableSpec` at line 3095 — only the two kind-named members are broken.)
